verdict.rationale: Linear's Loops let a user describe a recurring job in plain language, with no code, and trigger it on a schedule or on workspace events. The docs give one multi-step example: when a target date changes, a loop updates the launch plan and posts a Slack message. Multi-step behavior relies on agent interpretation of a natural-language description rather than a documented, controllable step-by-step builder, so only part of the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: an explicit multi-step workflow builder or documented step chaining and branching control, independent or hands-on corroboration that Loops reliably run multi-step automations, and documentation of the action types a loop can perform beyond the example.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can build multi-step automations without writing code

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams. They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
